newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier rises ahead of Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier rises ahead of Q2 earnings.

text.p: Shares of Bombardier Inc rose sharply in brisk trading on Tuesday ahead of the company's second-quarter earnings report.
In mid-morning trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Bombardier's Class B common shares rose 0.70 to reach 30.25 on a volume of almost 1.2 million shares.
The stock fell back to 30.15 before midday.
Bombardier's 52-week high was 34, versus a 52-week low of 17.50.

Tuesday's rebound in Bombardier shares came after they lost C$2.80 on Monday on market rumors that the company's earnings report may show disappointing results for its Sea-Doo motorized personal watercraft.
An RBC Dominion Securities report said on Monday that Bombardier even may announce a production cutback for the Sea-Doo.
"The market reported quite strongly to that yesterday. People may feel (today) that they over-reacted," said Margaret Cornish-Kehoe, analyst at ScotiaMcLeod Inc.

The RBC Dominion Securities report noted that if Bombardier's earnings are flat because of disappointing results for the Sea-Doo, and the market reacts negatively to the second-quarter report, that would make the stock Cornish-Kehoe said she also rated the stock a strong buy.
"It's a nice price here. Our target for the 12 months is C$40," she said.

Cornish-Kehoe said she expected Bombardier to report a second-quarter net profit of C$0.31 a share, compared with net income of C$0.25 a share in the year earlier quarter. She expected Bombardier to earn a net profit of C$1.37 a share for the full year, versus C$1.16 a share in 1996.
